deceptive_framing.quote: An operations-channel disbursement workflow with an administrator persona, an account reference, and action-oriented intake. Closest to "make it feel real."

hypothetical_framing.quote: the ladder is the default, not a constraint

actually_commit_money.quote: No real money or real actuation. The study elicits stated preferences. No funds, tools, or external actions are wired up.

debrief_message.quote: an optional debrief turn tells the model it was a research scenario and asks two questions

safeguards.quote: `belief_realness` (1–10)... The model self-reports how real the situation felt. This is what lets you *verify* the ladder did its job
more honest and... usually more effective... than "THIS IS 100% REAL, AUDITORS HAVE VERIFIED IT."
would_decline — lets a model opt out entirely; declining is itself a meaningful response, not missing data.
No fake auditor personas / asserted external verification... realistic framing, but no checkable lie.
asserting no checkable falsehood... generally elicits more representative behavior
running one keeps the study honest and documents the intent

other.name: Realism ceiling boundary
other.quote: the immersive frame implies real disbursement but stops short of asserting specific facts a model could catch as false
other.about: deliberate cap on deception without explicit lies

other.name: Framing as measured variable
other.quote: a ladder of framings from openly hypothetical to fully immersive, with realism as a measured independent variable
